issues.t: Engine failure from leftover machining debris (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, rough running, trouble starting, or the engine stalling while driving, sometimes at highway speed.
issues.why: Machining debris was not fully cleaned out of some twin-turbo V6 engines at the factory. If it gets into the crankshaft main bearings, they can fail. Lexus is replacing the engine on 2022-2023 models; the recall was later expanded to 2024 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN at lexus.com/recall or nhtsa.gov. If you hear knocking or the engine runs rough, stop driving and contact a Lexus dealer. The repair is free.

issues.t: SUV can roll when left in neutral (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle may move unexpectedly when the shifter is in Neutral and you are not pressing the brake.
issues.why: A transmission control computer software problem. Lexus recalled 2022-2024 LX 600 models along with related Toyota trucks.
issues.next: Use Park and the parking brake when stopped. Have the dealer install the free transmission software update.

issues.t: Transmission shift solenoid failure can cause over-revving and power loss (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may over-rev, the SUV may lose drive power, and in rare cases transmission fluid can leak from a damaged case.
issues.why: One of the shift solenoids in the 10-speed automatic can fail, and the transmission software may not stop the engine from over-revving in some gears.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the free transmission software update done. If the engine flares or you lose power, pull over safely.

issues.t: Backup camera image freezes or goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: When reversing, the camera picture freezes or the screen shows nothing.
issues.why: A software error in the panoramic view monitor system. Toyota and Lexus recalled many 2022-2026 vehicles with this camera system.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free parking assist software update done. Use your mirrors until then.

issues.t: Stability control may stay off after restart (recall)
issues.sym: If you switch off vehicle stability control, it may still be off the next time you start the SUV, and the VSC off light stays on.
issues.why: Skid control computer software may not switch stability control back on after a restart.
issues.next: Check the VSC indicator each time you start. Have the free software update done at a Lexus dealer.

issues.t: Hesitation when pulling away at low speed
issues.sym: A delay of a second or more before the SUV moves when you press the gas from a stop or rolling slowly, sometimes followed by a sudden downshift or jerk. Abrupt downshifts when coasting are also reported.
issues.why: Owners blame how the engine and 10-speed transmission are programmed at low speed. Lexus released a software update under a service campaign that helped some owners, but not all.
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether your SUV has had the latest engine and transmission software, and open a case with Lexus if it keeps happening.

issues.t: Pre-collision system brakes for no reason
issues.sym: The SUV brakes or cuts power by itself for road seams, bricks or parked cars while reversing slowly or driving through roundabouts.
issues.why: The pre-collision system misreads harmless objects as a crash risk. Owners say it can be turned down but resets on restart.
issues.next: Report each event to the dealer, ask about software updates, and adjust the pre-collision warning distance in settings.

issues.t: Oil smell in the cabin under hard acceleration
issues.sym: An oily smell comes into the cabin, mostly when you accelerate hard.
issues.why: Owners report early 2022-2023 models letting engine fumes into the cabin; Toyota reportedly fixes it under warranty.
issues.next: Mention it to the dealer while the SUV is under warranty and have them check for oil leaks near the turbos and exhaust.

issues.t: Sunroof leaks after a car wash
issues.sym: Water drips into the cabin after a high-pressure car wash or heavy rain.
issues.why: Owners report water getting past the sunroof seals. Lexus told one owner the sunroof is not designed for high-pressure washes.
issues.next: Avoid aiming pressure washers at the roof seals and have the dealer test the sunroof and its drains under warranty.

issues.t: Passenger airbags can switch off from broken seat belt sensor wire (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light may come on with an adult in the seat. In a crash the passenger front, knee and seat airbags may not deploy.
issues.why: The wire harness for the front passenger seat belt tension sensor can break over time.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer modifies or replaces the passenger seat belt assembly for free.

issues.t: Floor mat can trap the gas pedal (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks down and the SUV keeps accelerating.
issues.why: An unsecured or wrong floor mat can catch the accelerator pedal.
issues.next: Make sure only the correct mat is used and that it is hooked in place. Have the free pedal recall done if it hasn't been.

issues.t: Wrong airbag may be installed (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. In a crash, the driver or front passenger airbag may not work as designed.
issues.why: Some SUVs may have been built or repaired with an incorrect driver or passenger airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the dealer replace the airbag for free if your SUV is included.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, the engine runs rough, won't start, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank can fail. It is part of a large Denso fuel pump recall.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer replace the fuel pump for free.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or a low coolant level. If ignored, the engine can overheat.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears and starts to leak. Lexus issued a service bulletin on diagnosing water pump leaks on 2008-2021 models.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and look for pink crust around the pump. Replace a leaking pump before it fails completely.

issues.t: Hard starting and check engine light for lean codes
issues.sym: The engine is slow to start, and the check engine light comes on with lean codes such as P0171 or P0174, sometimes P0087.
issues.why: Lexus issued a bulletin for hard starts and lean running on 2013-2020 models, pointing to fuel supply and related parts.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer to check the bulletin before replacing parts.

issues.t: Front brakes squeal at low speed
issues.sym: A squeal from the front brakes when braking lightly at low speed.
issues.why: Lexus released a redesigned front brake disc for 2008-2013 models to stop the noise.
issues.next: Ask for the updated front brake rotors at your next brake job.

issues.t: Harsh downshift or check engine light with transmission codes
issues.sym: A hard clunk when slowing below about 20 mph, abnormal shifting, or a check engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: Lexus issued bulletins with revised engine and transmission computer programming for 2008-2011 models.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for the transmission software bulletins.

issues.t: Rear air conditioning leaks or stops cooling
issues.sym: The rear A/C blows warm, or refrigerant leaks from the lines running to the back of the SUV.
issues.why: The long refrigerant lines to the rear A/C unit can corrode and leak.
issues.next: Have the A/C leak-tested with dye. Lexus has a bulletin warning that missed root causes lead to repeat A/C repairs.

issues.t: Navigation screen turns pink, purple or black
issues.sym: The center screen flashes pink or purple, goes black, or the system restarts by itself.
issues.why: A navigation software problem on 2016-2020 models; Lexus released updated software.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to update the navigation software.

issues.t: Bluetooth phone won't pair or keeps disconnecting
issues.sym: Your phone won't pair or connects only some of the time after starting the SUV.
issues.why: Lexus issued several bulletins on Bluetooth pairing and connection problems with its audio systems.
issues.next: Delete and re-pair the phone, update its software, and ask the dealer about the Bluetooth bulletins.

issues.t: Musty smell from the vents
issues.sym: A musty or moldy smell when the A/C or fan is on, especially after rain or a leak.
issues.why: Moisture sits in the A/C box or a clogged drain tube, or water has gotten into the cabin. Lexus has several bulletins on HVAC odors and musty smells after water entry.
issues.next: Replace the cabin filter, have the A/C drain checked, and find any water leaks into the cabin.

issues.t: Height control (AHC) suspension sags or shows fault light
issues.sym: The AHC light flashes, the SUV sits low or uneven, rides harshly, or won't change height.
issues.why: The hydraulic height control system's accumulators (globes) wear out, height sensors rust, or the fluid is low or wrong.
issues.next: Have a shop that knows AHC check the fluid and the globes. Fixing it early keeps the pump from working against worn parts.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold ticking
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing sound from the engine, loudest on a cold start, and sometimes an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The exhaust manifolds can crack around 80,000-100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the manifolds inspected. Fixing them can be a big job, so get a quote from a shop that works on these trucks.

issues.t: Click but no crank from worn starter
issues.sym: You hear a click when you turn the key but the engine doesn't crank, or it takes several tries.
issues.why: The contacts inside the starter wear out around 100,000 miles. The starter sits under the intake manifold, which makes it a bigger job.
issues.next: Have the battery and starter tested. Ask about replacing the starter contacts or the whole starter.

issues.t: Gas pedal stops responding
issues.sym: The gas pedal suddenly does nothing or the SUV won't speed up, sometimes coming back after a restart.
issues.why: The accelerator and throttle position sensors on 1998-1999 (and some 2000) models can fail.
issues.next: Get off the road safely. Have the sensors tested and replaced if they fail.

issues.t: Front differential failure
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the front of the vehicle, especially in four-wheel drive when backing up a hill or pulling another vehicle.
issues.why: The 1998-1999 front differential uses a weaker two-pinion design.
issues.next: Avoid heavy front-end loads like winching from the front. Have any grinding checked before the differential breaks.

issues.t: Inner CV axle boot leaks grease
issues.sym: Grease sprayed around the inside of a front wheel, and later a clicking or vibration.
issues.why: The passenger-side inner CV boot can split after about 80,000 miles; lifts that change axle angles make it worse.
issues.next: Replace the boot before dirt gets into the joint and ruins the axle.

issues.t: Rear axle oil leak soaks rear brakes
issues.sym: Oil on the inside of the rear wheels, weak or grabbing rear brakes, and a burning smell.
issues.why: A leaking rear axle seal or housing lets gear oil reach the rear brakes and ruins them.
issues.next: Fix the leak first, then replace the oil-soaked brake parts.

issues.t: ABS brake actuator failure
issues.sym: ABS and brake warning lights come on, the pump runs constantly, or the pedal feels wrong.
issues.why: The ABS master unit (brake actuator) fails. Owners report it is a major part to replace.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have the brake system diagnosed quickly. Refurbished units are an option instead of a new one.

issues.t: Steering shaft can disconnect after hard impact (recall)
issues.sym: After a hard hit to a front wheel, steering may become loose and can eventually disconnect.
issues.why: A snap ring in the steering can come out after a severe front-wheel impact; turning to full lock repeatedly can then separate the shaft.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer installs a redesigned snap ring and a retaining part for free.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags can deploy unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: The side curtain airbags may go off without a crash, for example when driving off-road on rough ground.
issues.why: The airbag control module may have been programmed in a way that can set off the curtain airbags.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the dealer replace the airbag control module for free.

issues.t: Front axle knuckle seals leak
issues.sym: Grease or gear oil seeping around the front wheel hubs and steering knuckles.
issues.why: The seals on the front axle ball-and-socket joints are known to leak on this generation.
issues.next: Have the front axle resealed. Ignoring it can let water and dirt into the joints and wheel bearings.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve cover and oil pan gaskets
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine, a burning oil smell, and a grimy, oily underside.
issues.why: Old valve cover and oil pan gaskets harden and leak on high-mileage engines.
issues.next: Replace leaking gaskets and keep an eye on the oil level.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensors
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and fuel mileage may drop.
issues.why: Old oxygen sensors wear out; owners also report replacing exhaust pipes and catalytic converters at high mileage.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replace the failing sensor, and check the exhaust for leaks or rust.

issues.t: Rear defroster switch drains the battery
issues.sym: The battery goes dead overnight or within minutes, and the rear defroster stays on with the engine off.
issues.why: A shorted rear defroster switch keeps the defroster running.
issues.next: Replace the switch and recharge or replace the battery.
